description: I'm a Computer Science and Engineering graduate from Mozambique, passionate about AI, Machine Learning, software development, and data science. I have experience with Python, Java, React, and data analysis. I'm building NYELETI AI to explore satellite data and address environmental challenges. I'm looking for collaborators skilled in GIS, Remote Sensing, AI/ML, Python, and UI/UX design. Let's combine our skills to build innovative solutions with real-world impact!
summary: NYELETI AI turns two decades of NASA active-fire detections into one consistent burning-activity calendar. MODIS (2001–) and VIIRS (2012–) cannot be compared directly: over Mozambique, VIIRS reports about five times as many detections as MODIS. We train a LightGBM model that maps MODIS cell-day features onto the VIIRS S-NPP scale, add a climatological background for fires only VIIRS can see, and publish an HFAI activity index. An Isolation Forest flags unusual past periods. The web app (EN/PT) offers a map, calendar, harmonization metrics, anomalies, critical periods and PDF/CSV/GeoJSON exports. On the held-out year 2025, province-day HFAI RMSE falls from 122.6 (raw MODIS) to 65.0 (R² 0.88). All values come from NASA FIRMS; originals are never overwritten.

NYELETI AI is a web application that harmonizes NASA MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detections into one burning-activity calendar for any selected area of Mozambique (country, province, district, or a user-drawn polygon).

How it works

1. Download NASA FIRMS yearly country files (MODIS MCD14ML, VIIRS S-NPP VNP14IMGTML, VIIRS NOAA-20 VJ114IMGTML).

2. Clean and assign detections to a 5 km equal-area grid (EPSG:6933).

3. Build MODIS-informed cell-day features (cell + neighbours + previous/next day).

4. Train LightGBM models that predict VIIRS detection count and FRP from MODIS features (train 2012-2022, validation 2023-2024, independent test 2025).

5. Add a climatological background rate for cell-days where only VIIRS sees fire.

6. Compute the Harmonized Fire Activity Index (HFAI) and build daily calendars.

7. Flag unusual past periods with an Isolation Forest on seasonal features.

Benefits and impact

Gives fire managers, scientists and responders a continuous 2001-2025 view of burning activity on a single scale, with observed and estimated values always kept separate. On the held-out year 2025, province-day HFAI RMSE improves from 122.6 (raw MODIS) to 65.0 (R-squared 0.88).

Tools and stack

Python (Pandas, GeoPandas, LightGBM, scikit-learn, DuckDB), FastAPI, React + TypeScript, MapLibre GL, Plotly. Interface in English and Portuguese.

Limits

Cell-day skill is modest; MODIS gaps propagate into the harmonized series; values before 2012 are unverifiable estimates; anomalies are retrospective, not forecasts.

Super Intelligence acknowledgement

Coding assistance was used with Cursor (Composer) to accelerate implementation. All fire numbers come from NASA FIRMS experiments; metrics were produced by our evaluation scripts.
